smt-2021-guts-01.title: Half the perimeter
smt-2021-guts-01.body:
The sides satisfy $l^2+w^2=289$ and $lw=120$, so $(l+w)^2=289+240=529$ and $l+w=23$ (the pool is $8\times15$). Running around the edge of the pool, starting at opposite points, Rachel is half the perimeter, $l+w=23$ units, behind Joey. She gains $5$ units each second, so she catches him after $\frac{23}5$ seconds.

**Answer: $\frac{23}{5}$ seconds**

smt-2021-guts-02.title: Count cards
smt-2021-guts-02.body:
A pile with flipped value $v$ has $1+(12-v)=13-v$ cards. With flipped values $v_1,\dots,v_5$ the piles contain $65-(v_1+\cdots+v_5)$ cards, and together with the $4$ leftover cards this is all $52$. So $v_1+\cdots+v_5=65+4-52=17$.

**Answer: 17**

smt-2021-guts-03.title: Parity
smt-2021-guts-03.body:
Consider the grid distance (sum of the absolute coordinate differences) between two people. Each second both move one step, so this distance changes by $-2$, $0$ or $+2$: its parity never changes. To infect someone, an infected person must share a lattice point with them, i.e. be at distance $0$, which is even. But every other person starts at distance $3$ (odd) from the origin person, so can never be at distance $0$ from them. The same holds for anyone who might later become infected (they would have to be at even distance from someone), so no one else is ever infected: the number of newly infected people is $0$ (so the only infected person is the original one).

**Answer: 0**

smt-2021-guts-04.title: Areas
smt-2021-guts-04.body:
The circle has radius $1$ and is inscribed in the regular hexagon, so the hexagon's apothem is $1$ and its side is $\frac{2}{\sqrt3}$. Hexagon area $=\frac12\cdot\text{perimeter}\cdot\text{apothem}=\frac12\cdot6\cdot\frac2{\sqrt3}\cdot1=2\sqrt3$ mm$^2$. Diamond area $=\pi$. Cost $=100\pi+50(2\sqrt3-\pi)=50\pi+100\sqrt3$ dollars.

**Answer: $\$(50\pi+100\sqrt3)$**

smt-2021-guts-05.title: Complement
smt-2021-guts-05.body:
There are $900$ three-digit integers. Those with no $0$ and no $5$ have leading digit from $\{1,2,3,4,6,7,8,9\}$ ($8$ choices) and each other digit from the same $8$ digits: $8^3=512$. So $900-512=388$.

**Answer: 388**

smt-2021-guts-06.title: Two cases
smt-2021-guts-06.body:
Either $x+8=0$, giving $x=-8$ (both denominators are nonzero there), or the denominators are equal: $5x+7=7x+5$, giving $x=1$. The sum is $-8+1=-7$.

**Answer: $-7$**

smt-2021-guts-07.title: Sector minus triangle
smt-2021-guts-07.body:
$\angle AOC=135^\circ$ and $\angle AOD=67.5^\circ$. The region $ADE$ is the sector $AOD$ minus triangle $AOE$. Sector $AOD$ has area $\frac{67.5}{360}\cdot16\pi=3\pi$. Since $OA=OC$ and $OE$ bisects the apex angle, $E$ is the midpoint of $AC$, so $[AOE]=\frac12[AOC]=\frac12\cdot\frac12\cdot16\sin135^\circ=2\sqrt2$. Area $=3\pi-2\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $3\pi-2\sqrt2$**

smt-2021-guts-08.title: Binary representation
smt-2021-guts-08.body:
A bacterium added $k$ nights before the end becomes $2^k$ bacteria. So the final population is a sum of powers of $2$, one per added bacterium, and the fewest added bacteria is the fewest powers of $2$ summing to $2021$, which is the number of ones in its binary expansion. $2021=11111100101_2=1024+512+256+128+64+32+4+1$, which has $8$ ones.

**Answer: 8**

smt-2021-guts-09.title: Volume by slices
smt-2021-guts-09.body:
At height $z$ the cross-section is a disc of radius $\sqrt z$ and area $\pi z$. So $V=\int_0^5\pi z\,dz=\frac{25\pi}2$. At $5$ cubic froyos per second, the time is $\frac{25\pi/2}{5}=\frac{5\pi}2$ seconds.

**Answer: $\frac{5\pi}{2}$ seconds**

smt-2021-guts-09.title: Shells
smt-2021-guts-09.body:
Using cylindrical shells, $V=\int_0^{\sqrt5}2\pi r(5-r^2)\,dr=2\pi\left(\frac{5r^2}2-\frac{r^4}{4}\right)\Big|_0^{\sqrt5}=2\pi\left(\frac{25}{2}-\frac{25}4\right)=\frac{25\pi}2$, giving the same time.

**Answer: $\frac{5\pi}{2}$ seconds**

smt-2021-guts-10.title: Which houses have an odd number of packets
smt-2021-guts-10.body:
Odd-numbered houses are never visited by George (he visits multiples of even $m$). Pete adds one packet for each odd night $n$ dividing the house number $h$; for odd $h$ every divisor is odd, so house $h$ holds $d(h)$ packets, which is odd iff $h$ is a perfect square.

For even $h$, each odd divisor $n$ of $h$ gives an even divisor $2n$ of $h$, and George's visit on night $2n$ comes after Pete's drop on night $n$, so he removes a packet for each one dropped: no packets remain (each of George's removals finds a packet available, and any surplus visits find nothing).

So the houses with an odd number of packets are the odd squares $1^2,3^2,\dots,43^2$ ($43^2=1849<2021<45^2$): $22$ houses. Pete picks $3$ of them (in increasing order, so only the set matters): $\binom{22}{3}=1540$.

**Answer: 1540**

smt-2021-guts-11.title: Taxi-cab diamonds
smt-2021-guts-11.body:
In the taxi-cab metric the points reachable with a rope of length $r$ form a diamond $|x|+|y|\le r$. In quadrants I, II and IV the house is not in the way, so the goat reaches three full quarter-diamonds, each a right triangle with legs $\frac72$ and area $\frac12\left(\frac72\right)^2=\frac{49}8$: total $\frac{147}8$.

In quadrant III the house is in the way. The goat can go along the top of the house to the corner $(-2,0)$, using $2$ of the rope; the remaining $\frac32$ sweeps a triangle with legs $\frac32$ (area $\frac98$) to the left of the house. Symmetrically around the corner $(0,-2)$ below the house: another triangle of area $\frac98$. Going further around the corners $(-2,-1)$ and $(-1,-2)$ (rope used: $3$), the remaining $\frac12$ sweeps two triangles with legs $\frac12$ (area $\frac18$ each). Quadrant III contributes $2\cdot\frac98+2\cdot\frac18=\frac52=\frac{20}8$.

Total: $\frac{147}8+\frac{20}8=\frac{167}8$. (A numerical computation of the reachable region agrees.)

**Answer: $\frac{167}{8}$**

smt-2021-guts-12.title: Intersection condition
smt-2021-guts-12.body:
The vertex is $(0,c)$, so the circle has radius $|c|$: $x^2+y^2=c^2$. Substituting $y=ax^2+c$: $x^2+(ax^2+c)^2=c^2$, i.e. $x^2\left(a^2x^2+2ac+1\right)=0$. Besides $x=0$ there are solutions iff $a^2x^2=-(2ac+1)$ has a real solution with $x\ne0$, i.e. iff $2ac+1<0$. To have only the vertex, we need $2ac+1\ge0$, so $a\le-\frac1{2c}$ (note $c<0$). The maximum is $a=-\frac1{2c}$.

**Answer: $a=-\dfrac1{2c}$**

smt-2021-guts-13.title: Orderings and breaks
smt-2021-guts-13.body:
Write the five letters in a row in $5!=120$ ways, then decide independently for each of the $4$ gaps between consecutive letters whether there is a word break: $2^4=16$ ways. Total $120\cdot16=1920$. (Equivalently $120\sum_{k=0}^4\binom4k=120+480+720+480+120$.)

**Answer: 1920**

smt-2021-guts-14.title: Derangements
smt-2021-guts-14.body:
The number of derangements of $7$ objects is $7!\sum_{k=0}^7\frac{(-1)^k}{k!}=5040-5040+2520-840+210-42+7-1=1854$. The probability is $\frac{1854}{5040}=\frac{103}{280}$.

**Answer: $\frac{103}{280}$**

smt-2021-guts-15.title: Swept regions
smt-2021-guts-15.body:
Each lobe tip is at distance $3$ from the centre (a unit circle centred at distance $2$). As the spinner turns $60^\circ$, each tip sweeps a $60^\circ$ sector of the circle of radius $3$: $\frac16\pi\cdot9=\frac32\pi$ each, $\frac92\pi$ for the three. By symmetry, the rest of the swept region consists of three congruent pieces, each made of an equilateral triangle of side $2$ (area $\sqrt3$) together with two $120^\circ$ sectors of unit circles (area $\frac{\pi}3$ each), so each piece has area $\sqrt3+\frac{2\pi}{3}$ and the three have area $3\sqrt3+2\pi$.

Total: $\frac92\pi+2\pi+3\sqrt3=\frac{13\pi}2+3\sqrt3$. (A numerical computation of the swept region, built from the figure's geometry, gives $25.616\ldots=\frac{13\pi}2+3\sqrt3$.)

**Answer: $\frac{13\pi}{2}+3\sqrt3$**

smt-2021-guts-17.title: Reciprocal polynomial
smt-2021-guts-17.body:
The numbers $\frac1p,\frac1q,\frac1r$ are the roots of $x^3f(1/x)=3+2x+x^2+8x^3$, whose $x^2$ and $x^3$ coefficients are $1$ and $8$, so their sum is $-\frac18$.

**Answer: $-\frac18$**

smt-2021-guts-18.title: The first player loses only with two hands
smt-2021-guts-18.body:
The first player ends with three cards and the second with two, so the first player loses only if his hand is $\{1,2,3\}$ or $\{1,2,4\}$ (sums $6$ and $7$ against $9$ and $8$); every other three-card hand has sum at least $8>7$. So the first player tries to avoid these hands.

- If the $5$ is face up first, the first player takes it and cannot lose.
- If $1$ or $2$ is face up, the first player draws from the stack (taking it would help the losing hands), and the second player also draws from the stack to force him to take the face-up card at some point; the game depends only on the order of the stack. For the first player to end up with the $2$ (when $1$ is up) it must be in position $1$ or $3$ of the stack, probability $\frac12$, and then the $3$ or $4$ must be in the other odd position, probability $\frac23$: his loss probability is $\frac13$.
- If $3$ or $4$ is face up, the first player takes it. Then the second player wins only if he gets the $5$ and the other high card, which happens with probability $\frac13$.

Averaging over the five equally likely face-up cards: $\frac{4\cdot\frac13+0}{5}=\frac4{15}$. (An exhaustive minimax computation over all card orders confirms exactly $\frac4{15}$.)

**Answer: $\frac4{15}$**

smt-2021-guts-19.title: Mod 3
smt-2021-guts-19.body:
For $p>3$, $p^2\equiv1\pmod3$ and $2^p\equiv2\pmod3$ (odd exponent), so $3\mid2^p+p^2$ and it is composite. Checking $p=2$: $4+4=8$ (not prime); $p=3$: $8+9=17$ (prime). So the only such prime is $3$, and the sum is $3$.

**Answer: 3**

smt-2021-guts-20.title: Cycle colourings
smt-2021-guts-20.body:
The number of proper colourings of the cycle $C_n$ with $k$ colours is $(k-1)^n+(-1)^n(k-1)$. For $k=3$, $n=8$: $2^8+2=258$.

**Answer: 258**

smt-2021-guts-20.title: Recursion
smt-2021-guts-20.body:
Let $a_n$ be the number of proper colourings of an $n$-cycle with $3$ colours. Remove the last vertex $n$: if vertices $1$ and $n-1$ have different colours, the colour of $n$ is forced, giving $a_{n-1}$ colourings; if they have the same colour, vertex $n$ has $2$ choices and the rest is a colouring of an $(n-2)$-cycle, giving $2a_{n-2}$. So $a_n=a_{n-1}+2a_{n-2}$ with $a_2=6$, $a_3=6$. Then $a_4=18$, $a_5=30$, $a_6=66$, $a_7=126$, $a_8=258$.

**Answer: 258**

smt-2021-guts-21.title: Second derivative
smt-2021-guts-21.body:
$f'(x)=-\sin(\sin x)\cos x$ and $f''(x)=-\cos(\sin x)\cos^2x+\sin(\sin x)\sin x$. At $x=n\pi$, $\sin x=0$ and $\cos^2x=1$, so $f''(n\pi)=-1$. There are $2022$ terms, so the sum is $-2022$.

**Answer: $-2022$**

smt-2021-guts-22.title: Substitute $k=A-\frac1A$
smt-2021-guts-22.body:
$f(x)=(3x^2-4)(x-k)$, $f'(x)=9x^2-6kx-4$ with roots $x_{1,2}=\frac{k\mp\sqrt{k^2+4}}{3}$. The local maximum is at $x_1$ and the local minimum at $x_2$, and a direct computation gives $f(x_1)-f(x_2)=\frac49\left(k^2+4\right)^{3/2}$ (for $k=0$: $f=3x^3-4x$, extrema at $x=\mp\frac23$ with values $\pm\frac{16}9$, difference $\frac{32}9=\frac49\cdot8$ ✓). This is smallest when $k=0$, i.e. $A-\frac1A=0$, so $A=\pm1$.

**Answer: $A=\pm1$**

smt-2021-guts-23.title: Group of the square
smt-2021-guts-23.body:
The $7$ moves are the non-identity elements of the dihedral group $D_4$. After two moves $m_1m_2$ the square is not at the original position unless $m_2=m_1^{-1}$ (each $m_1$ has exactly one such $m_2$). If it is not at the start after two moves, exactly one third move returns it, and it is a valid (non-identity) move. So the count is the number of pairs $(m_1,m_2)$ with $m_2\ne m_1^{-1}$: $49-7=42$.

**Answer: 42**

smt-2021-guts-24.title: Digit equation
smt-2021-guts-24.body:
Write the number as $abcde$. The condition is $10a+b=a+b+c+d+e$, i.e. $9a=c+d+e$, so $c+d+e\in\{9,18,27\}$ (it is positive and at most $27$). Number of digit triples $(c,d,e)$: sum $9$: $\binom{11}2=55$; sum $18$: $\binom{20}2-3\binom{10}2=190-135=55$; sum $27$: $1$. Total $111$, then $a$ is determined ($a=1,2,3$) and $b$ is any of $10$ digits: $111\cdot10=1110$.

**Answer: 1110**

smt-2021-guts-25.title: Use $\sin 2\pi=0$
smt-2021-guts-25.body:
The Taylor series of $\sin x$ at $x=2\pi$ gives $0=\sin2\pi=\sum_i\frac{(2\pi)^{4i+1}}{(4i+1)!}-\sum_i\frac{(2\pi)^{4i+3}}{(4i+3)!}$. So the numerator equals $\sum_i\frac{(2\pi)^{4i+3}}{(4i+3)!}=(2\pi)^2\sum_i\frac{(2\pi)^{4i+1}}{(4i+3)!}$, which is $(2\pi)^2$ times the denominator. The ratio is $4\pi^2$.

**Answer: $4\pi^2$**

smt-2021-guts-26.title: Right angles at $E$ and $F$
smt-2021-guts-26.body:
$AC=8$ is a diameter, so $\angle ABC=\angle AEC=\angle AFC=\angle ADC=90^\circ$. $BC=\sqrt{64-36}=2\sqrt7$ and $DC=\sqrt{64-49}=\sqrt{15}$. With $\alpha=\angle EAC=\frac12\angle BAC$: $AE=8\cos\alpha$, $EC=8\sin\alpha$, so $[AEC]=\frac12\cdot64\sin\alpha\cos\alpha=16\sin2\alpha=16\sin\angle BAC=16\cdot\frac{BC}{AC}=\frac{AC\cdot BC}{4}$. Likewise $[AFC]=\frac{AC\cdot DC}4$. 

So the area is $\frac14AC(BC+DC)=\frac{8(2\sqrt7+\sqrt{15})}{4}=4\sqrt7+2\sqrt{15}$.

**Answer: $4\sqrt7+2\sqrt{15}$**

smt-2021-guts-27.title: Area formula
smt-2021-guts-27.body:
By Vieta $r+s=a$ and $rs=8$. The area of the triangle with vertices $(r,0),(0,s),(t,t)$ is $\frac12\left|(-r)(t)-s(t-r)\right|=\frac12\left|rs-(r+s)t\right|=\frac{|8-at|}2$. Setting this equal to $2021$ gives $|at-8|=4042$, so $at=4050$ (the other case $at=-4034$ is impossible for positive integers). Now $4050=2\cdot3^4\cdot5^2$, and $a+t$ is smallest when the two factors are closest to $\sqrt{4050}\approx63.6$: $54\cdot75=4050$ gives $129$ (the next pair, $50\cdot81$, gives $131$). Both $a=54$ and $a=75$ give distinct real roots ($a^2>32$). The minimum is $129$.

**Answer: 129**

smt-2021-guts-28.title: Shift
smt-2021-guts-28.body:
Let $q(y)=p\left(y-\frac{21}{4}\right)$, which has a double root at $y=0$, so $q(y)=y^2r(y)$ for a quadratic $r$. Then $p(x)-1344x$ becomes $q(y)-1344\left(y-\frac{21}4\right)=q(y)-1344y+7056$, and its double roots in $y$ are (integer $-\frac14$)$+\frac{21}{4}$ = integers. So $q(y)-1344y+7056=(y-c)^2(y-d)^2$ for integers $c,d$. Since $q$ has no constant or linear term, comparing these terms: $c^2d^2=7056$ and $-2cd(c+d)=-1344$, i.e. $cd=\pm84$ and $cd(c+d)=672$. If $cd=84$ then $c+d=8$, which has no real $c,d$. If $cd=-84$ then $c+d=-8$, so $c,d$ are the roots of $t^2+8t-84=0$: $6$ and $-14$. The double roots in $x$ are $6-\frac{21}4=\frac34$ and $-14-\frac{21}4=-\frac{77}4$.

**Answer: $\frac34$ and $-\frac{77}4$**

smt-2021-guts-29.title: Trails in $K_4$
smt-2021-guts-29.body:
The path may visit $A,B,C,D$ repeatedly (no edge twice) and then ends with a single step to $E$ (it cannot visit $E$ earlier). So the count equals the number of trails (no repeated edge) starting at $A$ in the complete graph on $A,B,C,D$, of any length, including length $0$ (the last step to $E$ is then the edge from wherever the trail ended to $E$, always unused).

Counting trails from $A$ by length: $1,3,6,12,18,18$ for lengths $0,\dots,5$ (length $6$ would require all six edges and an Euler trail, impossible because $K_4$ has four odd-degree vertices). Total $1+3+6+12+18+18=58$.

**Answer: 58**

smt-2021-guts-30.title: Cauchy-Schwarz
smt-2021-guts-30.body:
By Cauchy-Schwarz, $\sum\frac{\sqrt{a_n}}{2^n}\le\sqrt{\sum a_n}\sqrt{\sum\frac1{4^n}}=\sqrt4\cdot\sqrt{\frac13}=\frac{2}{\sqrt3}=\frac{2\sqrt3}3$. Equality holds when $\sqrt{a_n}\propto\frac1{2^n}$, i.e. $a_n=\frac{12}{4^n}$ (then $\sum a_n=12\cdot\frac13=4$).

**Answer: $\frac{2\sqrt3}{3}$**

smt-2021-guts-31.title: Sophie Germain and telescoping
smt-2021-guts-31.body:
$x^4+4=(x^2+2x+2)(x^2-2x+2)=\left((x+1)^2+1\right)\left((x-1)^2+1\right)$. So $f(4k-1)=\left((4k)^2+1\right)\left((4k-2)^2+1\right)$ and $f(4k-3)=\left((4k-2)^2+1\right)\left((4k-4)^2+1\right)$, giving $\frac{f(4k-1)}{f(4k-3)}=\frac{(4k)^2+1}{(4k-4)^2+1}$. The product telescopes to $\frac{8084^2+1}{0^2+1}=8084^2+1=65351057$, with remainder $57$ modulo $1000$.

**Answer: 57**

smt-2021-guts-32.title: Power sums
smt-2021-guts-32.body:
The angles $\theta=\frac\pi9,\frac{5\pi}9,\frac{7\pi}9$ satisfy $\cos3\theta=\frac12$, so $x_i=\cos\theta_i$ are the three roots of $4x^3-3x=\frac12$, i.e. $x^3=\frac34x+\frac18$. Let $S_n=\sum x_i^n$. Then $S_n=\frac34S_{n-2}+\frac18S_{n-3}$. We have $S_0=3$, $S_1=0$ (no $x^2$ term), $S_2=0^2-2\left(-\frac34\right)=\frac32$. Then $S_3=\frac34\cdot0+\frac18\cdot3=\frac38$, $S_4=\frac34\cdot\frac32+\frac18\cdot0=\frac98$, $S_5=\frac34\cdot\frac38+\frac18\cdot\frac32=\frac{15}{32}$, $S_6=\frac34\cdot\frac98+\frac18\cdot\frac38=\frac{57}{64}$, $S_7=\frac34\cdot\frac{15}{32}+\frac18\cdot\frac98=\frac{63}{128}$.

**Answer: $\frac{63}{128}$**

smt-2021-guts-33.title: Use the reflection
smt-2021-guts-33.body:
$C$ is the reflection of $A$, so $C=(4,5)$, and $A$, $C$ are on opposite sides of $y=x$, each at distance $\frac1{\sqrt2}$. Hence $[ABCD]=\frac12\cdot BD\cdot\frac2{\sqrt2}=\frac{BD}{\sqrt2}=|x_B-x_D|$. The line $\ell_i$ through $(5,4)$ with slope $m_i$ meets $y=x$ at $x=\frac{4-5m_i}{1-m_i}=5-\frac1{1-m_i}$. So $[ABCD]=\left|\frac1{1-m_1}-\frac1{1-m_2}\right|$.

From the first condition $m_2=\frac{5m_1-4}{4m_1+5}$, so $1-m_2=\frac{9-m_1}{4m_1+5}$ and $1+m_2^2=\frac{41(1+m_1^2)}{(4m_1+5)^2}$. The second condition becomes $(1+m_1^2)^2=(1-m_1)^2(9-m_1)^2$, so $1+m_1^2=\pm(1-m_1)(9-m_1)$. The plus sign gives $m_1=\frac45$, $m_2=0$, which is excluded. The minus sign gives $m_1^2-5m_1+5=0$, i.e. $1+m_1^2=-(1-m_1)(9-m_1)$.

Then $\frac1{1-m_1}-\frac1{1-m_2}=\frac1{1-m_1}-\frac{4m_1+5}{9-m_1}=\frac{(9-m_1)-(4m_1+5)(1-m_1)}{(1-m_1)(9-m_1)}=\frac{4(1+m_1^2)}{(1-m_1)(9-m_1)}=-4$. So the area is $4$ (for both roots $m_1=\frac{5\pm\sqrt5}2$ with $m_2>0$).

**Answer: 4**

smt-2021-guts-34.title: Closed forms and CRT
smt-2021-guts-34.body:
Pairing consecutive terms, $S(2m,2)=\sum_{k=1}^m\left((2k)^2-(2k-1)^2\right)=\sum(4k-1)=m(2m+1)$, so $S(1010,2)=\frac{1010\cdot1011}{2}=505\cdot1011=510555$ and $S(2020,2)=1010\cdot2021$. Also $S(2m,4)=S(2m,2)\left(2S(2m,2)-1\right)$ (both sides are quartic polynomials in $m$ that agree at $m=0,\dots,4$, e.g. $S(2,4)=15=3\cdot5$ and $S(4,4)=190=10\cdot19$).

Let $T=S(2020,2)=1010\cdot2021$. Modulo $505$: $T\equiv0$, so $S(2020,4)\equiv0$. Modulo $1011$: $1010\equiv-1$ and $2021\equiv-1$, so $T\equiv1$ and $S(2020,4)\equiv1\cdot(2-1)=1$. Now $505t\equiv1\pmod{1011}$: since $505\cdot2=1010\equiv-1$, $t\equiv-2\equiv1009$. So $S(2020,4)\equiv505\cdot1009=509545\pmod{510555}$ (and $505\cdot1009$ is between $0$ and $510555$).

**Answer: 509545**

smt-2021-guts-35.title: Structure and enumeration
smt-2021-guts-35.body:
No two even numbers can be adjacent (their gcd is at least $2$), and there are $6$ evens among $12$ positions on the circle, so evens and odds alternate. The only other forbidden adjacencies are between an odd number and an even number sharing a factor: $3$ and $9$ with $6$ and $12$, and $5$ with $10$ (the other pairs are coprime).

Fixing the position of $1$ to remove rotations, an exhaustive enumeration of all valid placements gives $N=7776=6^5$ (counting an arrangement and its mirror image as different), so $\frac N{144}=54$.

**Answer: 54**

smt-2021-guts-36.title: Integrate the arctangent series
smt-2021-guts-36.body:
$\binom{2n}2=n(2n-1)$. Integrate $\arctan x=x-\frac{x^3}3+\frac{x^5}5-\cdots$ from $0$ to $1$: $\int_0^1\arctan x\,dx=\frac12\left(\frac1{1\cdot1}-\frac1{2\cdot3}+\frac1{3\cdot5}-\cdots\right)$, since the integral of $\frac{(-1)^{n-1}x^{2n-1}}{2n-1}$ is $\frac{(-1)^{n-1}}{2n(2n-1)}$. Hence the series is $2\int_0^1\arctan x\,dx$. By parts, $\int_0^1\arctan x\,dx=\left[x\arctan x-\frac12\ln(1+x^2)\right]_0^1=\frac\pi4-\frac{\ln2}2$. So the sum is $\frac\pi2-\ln2$.

**Answer: $\frac\pi2-\ln2$**
